question: Let $A=\{1,2,3,4\}$ and let $f:A\to A$ be one-one. Show that $f$ must also be onto.
explanation:
Consequence of the one-one property
The set $A$ contains four elements. Since $f$ is one-one, the images of the four distinct elements of $A$ must be four distinct elements of the co-domain $A$.

Comparison with the co-domain
The co-domain itself contains exactly four elements. Therefore, the four distinct images must exhaust all the elements of $A$.

Onto criterion
Thus, every element of the co-domain is the image of some element of the domain.

Conclusion
Hence, $f$ is onto.

options.A: $f$ need not be onto because one-one functions may leave elements of $A$ without pre-images
options.B: $f$ is onto only when $f(a)=a$ for every $a\in A$
options.C: $f$ is onto because four distinct domain elements have four distinct images that exhaust the four-element co-domain
options.D: $f$ cannot be onto because its domain and co-domain are the same set
